blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The canonical Ethereum implementation exposes owner-only addBlackList, removeBlackList, destroyBlackFunds, pause, and unpause functions. Tether's current Token Terms separately reserve the issuer's power to freeze Tether Tokens. This is a verified issuer and token freeze mechanism, not a classification inference.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USDT has issuer-native deployments on Tether-supported protocols and third-party representations on other networks. This review confirms only the contracts listed in Tether's supported-protocol registry as native issuance; USDT0 and every other unverified route remain conservatively unresolved at deployment level. 2026-07-20 cohort dc-1 pass: resolved the flagged non-native route controls with on-chain reads (token identity + controller/owner); see per-row reviewNote evidence. 2026-07-20 cohort cur-1 pass: resolved the five remaining unresolved routes (Sui Bridge, Injective Peggy, Corn USDT0, Katana Vault Bridge, HyperCore USDT0) from chain, LCD and explorer reads; see per-row reviewNote evidence.

routes.reviewNote: Resolved on-chain 2026-07-20 from Sui mainnet fullnode reads: CoinMetadata for 0x375f70cf...::usdt::USDT returns name 'Tether', symbol USDT, 6 decimals, description 'Bridged Tether token'; the coin package object is Immutable and its usdt module exposes no entry functions, so the TreasuryCap was escrowed at publish. The Sui Bridge shared object 0x...09 (package 0x...0b) holds it: BridgeInner.treasury.id_token_type_map entry 4 maps to 375f70cf...::usdt::USDT, and the bridge committee carries 96 registered members with 9133/10000 voting power (bridge_version 1, paused=false). Sui-side minting therefore requires threshold committee attestation of an Ethereum-side lock, not a Tether mint.
